title: Election denier Tina Peters to be hired as elections consultant in conservative California county
text: Tina Peters in Hudson, Colorado, in February 2023. Photograph: David Zalubowski/AP View image in fullscreen Tina Peters in Hudson, Colorado, in February 2023. Photograph: David Zalubowski/AP The fight to vote California Election denier Tina Peters to be hired as elections consultant in conservative California county Shasta county, hotbed of US election denialism movement, set to appoint ex-Colorado clerk who served prison term The fight to vote is supported by About this content Dani Anguiano in Chico, California and Sam Levine in New York Mon 17 Aug 2026 20.05 EDT First published on Mon 17 Aug 2026 17.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A northern California county that has become a hotbed of activism for those who sow doubts about the reliability of voting machines plans to hire Tina Peters, the prominent Colorado election denier recently released from prison, to work on elections. Clint Curtis , the top election official in Shasta county, told the Guardian he plans to hire Peters as a consultant to replace Brent Turner, his top deputy, who has been on medical leave. He said Peters would not have access to the county’s voting system and did not directly respond when asked

Утверждается, что журналистам удалось обнаружить десять объектов с новыми стартовыми позициями для БПЛА большой дальности. «Некоторые из этих баз уже используются для нанесения ударов по Украине, а их близость к границе способствует массированным воздушным атакам, наносимым мимо ослабевающей противовоздушной обороны Киева», — говорится в тексте. Издание пишет, что «быстро развивающиеся технологии могут быть использованы против Европы в случае войны, поскольку некоторые из российских баз размещают самые мощные беспилотники в зоне досягаемости Варшавы». По оценке The Telegraph, потенциальная дальность полета таких дронов составляет почти 1000 км. На одной из баз, утверждает газета, предусмотрено хранение более 1000 БПЛА. title: Trump says Kim Jong-un has responded to his overtures when asked about scaling back US drills with South Korea – as it happened
text: 14.15 EDT Trump says Kim Jong-un has responded to his overtures but doesn't offer details Donald Trump has ⁠said that ​ North Korean leader ⁠ Kim Jong-un ⁠has ​responded ‌to his overtures ‌after he ‌ordered the US to scale back military ‌exercises with South ​Korea . Speaking ‌to reporters in the Oval ‌Office, Trump was asked why Kim had not responded to his overtures. Trump shot back at the reporter: “How do you know he hasn’t responded?” The reporter then asked again if he had. “ Um, yeah he has, ” Trump said. Asked what stage the conversations with Kim were at, Trump said “ it’s very positive ”, but provided no further detail. He added: Kim Jong-un has always ​treated ​me with great ​respect and we met ​on numerous ‌occasions, ​actually ​two primary occasions, spoken and spent time. I understand him. He understands me. Their relationship was ‌a dominant theme during Trump’s first term, including a ​ series of meetings between them, but has received less emphasis in his second ⁠term.
